Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback (2505.02820v3) · paper method: The tested feedback protocol uses one feedback element per complete text-rendered agent trajectory; direct step-level/live feedback, generated programmatic metric evaluators and dense-reward reinforcement learning are future directions rather than demonstrated outcomes of this protocol.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback (2505.02820v3) · paper method: AutoLibra uses 197 CoGym end-user trajectories with feedback and author-expert feedback for other environments; five paper authors serve as expert annotators. For Sotopia, WebArena and WebVoyager, it annotates 100 GPT-4-based trajectories each and holds out 20% for the Section 4 analysis.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback (2505.02820v3) · paper method: The described pipeline uses GPT-4o to ground feedback into signed behavioral aspects, o3-mini high to cluster aspects into metrics, and o3-mini medium to rate trajectories +1, −1 or N/A on those metrics; metrics include definitions plus positive/negative examples.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback (2505.02820v3) · paper method: For each validated step and task, the authors sample 40 instances for binary human judgment of complete correctness; Table 1 averages 0.95 for grounding, 0.92 for LLM judging and 0.90 for meta-evaluation across five environments. Behavior clustering is not directly manually validated because processing over 400 aspects was considered too costly.
